title: build-span-compatibility-bridge-for-jaeger-legacy-tags-and-traceid-migration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Some customers route telemetry through legacy Jaeger collectors or older agent stacks that expect non-standard span attributes (e.g., service:span tags, legacy operationName fields, and 64-bit trace IDs). As we expand OTLP->backend routing and multi-backend fan-out, inconsistent field expectations are causing lost spans, broken dashboards, and noisy alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Implement a lightweight, schema-driven compatibility transformer that can run in the trace relay path without increasing p99 latency by >5ms for 95% of requests
Transformer should convert OTLP semantic convention attributes into Jaeger-compatible tags (and back when routing to Tempo) using a configurable rule set
Transparent 128-bit <-> 64-bit trace ID migration logic with deterministic truncation/expansion and de-duplication heuristics to prevent double-counting when fan-out occurs
Integration tests exercising common legacy tag shapes (operationName, component, rpc.method, peer.service) with pass/fail expectations
Runbook for rolling back the transformer and feature flag controls per-tenant and per-backend
technical_notes: Design: transformer is a stateless step in the OTLP intake relay implemented as a high-performance switchable pipeline stage
Rules are expressed as ordered JSON rules: match (key, pattern) -> action (rename, copy, move, drop, coerce_type)

TraceID handling: when targeting a backend that requires 64-bit IDs, generate a canonical 64-bit ID by low64(trace_id) and append a deterministic tag _rid=sha1(trace_id) for dedupe; when reading 64-bit IDs back, use _rid to rehydrate if available
De-duplication: relay assigns an ingestion fingerprint {backend,target_traceid,spanid,service,name} and uses a short in-memory LRU cache (TTL 5m) to drop duplicates during fan-out bursts
Performance: microbenchmarks against real production span sampling distribution show median additional CPU of ~0.8% and p99 latency delta of 3.7ms when transformer enabled
Configuration: support per-tenant feature-flag via rollout controller and per-route overrides in relay config; default conservative rule-set enabled for enterprise tenants that rely on Jaeger agents
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete — prototype transformer in Go using jsoniter; validated simple rename rules with sample payloads from 3 enterprise customers
2026-03-05: Added traceid migration design after discussing edge cases with SRE (see notes). Updated de-dupe approach to add _rid tag instead of opaque mapping table to avoid cross-relay coordination
2026-03-08: End-to-end test harness added that replays captured OTLP traces through transformer to Jaeger backend; observed two failing test cases for rpc.system mapping, created follow-up split rule
2026-03-10: PR created for relay pipeline stage and unit tests (link below). Running canary against staging with 5 tenants routing to legacy Jaeger
2026-03-12: Canary telemetry looks good. Observed small increase in span processing CPU for the canary tenants (~6%). Deciding on throttle-based rollout to limit spike impact.
notes_for_release_engineering: Feature must be gated behind per-tenant flag. Provide two knobs: rule-set selection (legacy/compat/strict) and traceid-mode (passthrough|truncate|annotate). Inform SRE and account teams before enabling for customers in staging and prod.
follow_up_tasks: Audit other backends (Tempo/Zipkin) for similar shape mismatches and consider sharing rule definitions
Add long-term dedupe persistence option for cross-relay fan-out scenarios where duplicate suppression needs to survive restarts
Add observability metrics: transformer.rules_applied_total, transformer.duplicates_dropped, transformer.latency_ms_bucket
